keys.statement: Choose an acid resin by its temperature limit: the review gives about 140 C for Amberlyst 15 and up to 190 C for Amberlyst 70. That limit bounds the temperature, and so the pressure, of a reactive zone.

decisions.obstacle: Resins lose acid groups when too hot.
decisions.mechanism: Each resin has a maximum service temperature.
decisions.operation: Match the resin to the reactive-zone temperature.
decisions.expected_change: A catalyst that survives the column conditions.

keys.statement: Esterification is equilibrium-limited, so removing water continuously (reactive distillation, or a pervaporation or nanofiltration membrane in the reactor) raises conversion at milder conditions.

decisions.mechanism: Removing a product shifts the equilibrium.
decisions.operation: Integrate water removal with the reaction.

keys.statement: For water-removal membranes, zeolite-coated ceramics (LTA or MFI type) withstand heat and chemicals better than polymer films. A polyvinyl alcohol membrane is reported to lose up to 35% of its permeability in 1000 h.

decisions.obstacle: Membranes degrade in hot reactive media.
decisions.mechanism: Inorganic supports resist swelling and attack.
decisions.operation: Prefer ceramic zeolite membranes for hot organic acid service.
limits: Ceramic membranes are noted as prone to cracking at large scale (Section 8.1).

keys.statement: Homogeneous mineral-acid catalysts are active but corrode equipment, cannot be recovered and add purification steps. Solid acid catalysts avoid these drawbacks.

decisions.obstacle: A dissolved acid catalyst stays in the product.
decisions.mechanism: A solid catalyst stays in the reactor.
decisions.operation: Prefer a solid acid catalyst where its temperature limit allows.
decisions.expected_change: No acid removal step, less corrosion.
